title: SLO Investigation Czar Process and Customer Signal Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:

This document defines the SLO Investigation Czar role, the standardized lifecycle for SLO-regression incidents, templates for internal and customer signalling, and a compact game-day checklist for practicing the flow. The goal is to reduce time-to-action for SLO degradations, standardize messaging, and ensure reproducible investigations and post-incident learning.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to any service with a published SLO on the Redwood status page and SLO dashboard (all production models, API gateway, routing, and datastore services).
- Intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, incident commanders, and customer-facing teams (CS/Support/AMs).
- Complements existing incident runbooks; this focuses on SLO regressions (silent failures, latency/error drift, and systemic skews).

Key definitions:
- SLO: Service Level Objective (e.g., 99.95% availability, p99 latency <= 300ms).
- SRE Alert: An automated alert tied to SLI thresholds (see Alert thresholds table).
- SLO Regression: A sustained violation of an SLO for >= 5 minutes or a short but high-impact breach (see severity table).
- SLO Investigation Czar (Czar): Designated role that centralizes triage coordination and customer signal decisions for SLO regressions.

Role: SLO Investigation Czar (summary)
- Primary responsibilities:
  - Own the investigation lifecycle for the SLO regression until the incident is transitioned to standard incident-response or resolved.
  - Make the “signal/no-signal” decision for customer-facing communications.
  - Coordinate evidence collection and the post-incident analysis scope.
- Who can be Czar:
  - On-call SRE, SRE team lead, or senior service owner. Rotation: Czar is assigned dynamically by the on-call rotation (see assignment rules).
- Escalation: If Czar cannot make progress within 20 minutes, escalate to Incident Commander (IC) or the cross-team bridge.

Alert thresholds and severity mapping (table)
- | Alert name | Trigger | Initial severity | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | slo-error-spike | error_rate_5m > 0.5% AND increase >= 3x baseline | sev-2 | Persisting >10m => escalate to Czar |
  | slo-latency-degrade | p99_latency_5m > 350ms | sev-2 | If client-facing latency regressions affect charts, escalate immediately |
  | slo-availability-drop | availability_1h < 99.9% | sev-1 | Potential major incident if customers impacted |
  | slo-silent-failure | 1+ dependent SLI missing/reporting-null | sev-1 | Investigate telemetry pipeline first |

Assignment rules (brief)
1) Alert fires -> primary on-call for the service receives page.
2) If SLO alert meets "investigation" criteria (see thresholds), page also tags the Czar rotation channel.
3) Primary on-call attempts quick mitigation (1–3 minutes). If not resolved, the on-call or Czar declares SLO Investigation in the internal incident channel and follows steps below.

SLO Investigation lifecycle (step-by-step)
1. Declare: post the SLO Investigation header to the service channel and the SRE bridge with:
   - Incident token: SLO-YYYYMMDD-<short-id>
   - Short description (one sentence)
   - Czar assigned (name) and current on-call
   Example: /msg #sre-bridge "SLO-20260214-73: p99 latency for embeddings-api > 350ms. Czar: Avery Chen. Initial triage started."

2. Rapid triage (0–10 minutes):
   - Verify alert correctness (missing SLIs, noisy metric).
   - Check rollout and recent deploys (git tags, infra changes) using:
     - git log --oneline --since='1 hour' services/embeddings-api
     - rollouts list --service embeddings-api --since 2h
   - Snapshot top-5 traces around 5xx and high-latency requests.
   - If root cause is obvious and fix is <15 minutes, perform mitigation and document change in the channel.

3. Escalate to Incident (10–20 minutes):
   - If triage finds systemic impact, customer-visible error, datastore outage, or mitigation >15m, promote to full incident and call Incident Commander.
   - The Czar continues as SLO lead alongside the IC.

4. Evidence collection (parallel):
   - Gather the following artifacts and attach to the incident channel and ticketing system:
     - SLI timeseries (raw) for 1h/6h/24h windows.
     - P95/P99 histograms, error logs, and top trace IDs.
     - Recent deploy manifest and config diffs.
     - Affected customer list (from routing and tokens).

5. Signal decision (customer-facing):
   - Czar must decide whether to post to the public status page and/or proactively contact affected customers. Decision criteria:
     - Do customers see failed requests or substantial UX disruption? -> Post to status and notify customer success.
     - Is degradation below customer-visible thresholds and transient (<15m)? -> Internal-only update.
   - If posting, use the standard templates in the Templates section.

6. Resolution & handoff:
   - When SLO returns to normal for a sustained window (default 30 minutes for latency; 1 hour for availability), the Czar marks the incident as resolved.
   - Create follow-up tasks for root cause analysis (RCA), regression tests, and rollout gating.

7. Post-incident analysis (within 3 business days):
   - Czar authors a concise RCA focused on the SLO vector and the decision timeline. Use the Postmortem template below.

Templates
- Short internal header (copy into Slack/bridge):
  "[SLO-{{incident_id}}] {{service}} - {{one_line}} | Czar: {{name}} | Status: TRIAGE/ESCALATED/RESOLVED"

- Status page template (public)
  - Title: "Partial service degradation — {{service}}"
  - Body: "We are aware of an issue impacting {{service}} causing increased latency and errors. Our SRE team is investigating (Incident {{incident_id}}). If you rely on {{feature}}, you may see timeouts or slower responses. We will post updates every 30 minutes or when there is a material change."
  - Impact field: "Latency increase for API calls to {{endpoint}} affecting some customers in {{region}}."
  - Resolution/next steps: "Normal service has been restored. We continue to monitor. A follow-up summary will be published within 72 hours."

- Customer proactive email template (short)
  Subject: "Redwood status — temporary service degradation affecting {{service}} ({{incident_id}})"
  Body: "Hello {{customer_name}},

We’re investigating a degradation affecting {{service}} which may cause slower responses or occasional errors. Our SRE team is working to resolve this. We will follow up with updates on progress and mitigation steps. If you have specific concerns or are experiencing critical failures, reply to this email and we’ll prioritize a dedicated follow-up.

Update cadence: every 30 minutes or sooner for material changes.

Sincerely,
Redwood SRE Team"

Runbook snippets and useful commands
- Check recent deploys and abort if needed:
  - rollout status --service {{service}} --last 2h
  - rollout abort --service {{service}} --id {{deploy_id}}
- Snapshot SLIs (example PromQL):
  - p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - error rate: sum(rate(requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
- Trace extraction (example):
  - otel-cli fetch --service={{service}} --time=5m --top=10 > traces-{{incident_id}}.json

Game-day checklist (30–60 minute practice cadence)
1) Pre-game prep (1 day before): ensure a current SLO dashboard link is pinned and the Czar rotation is populated.
2) Inject: simulate a p99 latency spike on a non-prod replica (use chaos runner).
3) Run: follow the lifecycle with a 20-minute cap for the Czar to declare signal or no-signal.
4) Communication: practice status page update and one proactive customer email.
5) Retro: capture lessons, update SLO thresholds if test reveals false positives.

Postmortem template (minimum required fields)
- Title: SLO-{{incident_id}} — {{service}} SLO regression postmortem\- Summary (1–2 sentences)\- Timeline (UTC timestamps)\- Impact (who and what)\- Root cause (concise)\- Corrective actions and owners (with due dates)\- Preventive measures (tests, alerts, runbook changes)\- Evidence (links to dashboards, traces, deploy manifests)

Governance and metrics of the process
- KPIs to track process health:
  - Mean time to Czar assignment (target < 2 minutes)
  - Time to first mitigation (target < 10 minutes for sev-2)
  - Fraction of SLO alerts promoted to incidents (baseline 8%)
  - Postmortem completion rate within 5 business days (target 90%)
- Quarterly review: SRE leadership reviews 5 anonymized SLO incidents to surface trends and SLO tuning opportunities.

Decision log (examples of past rationale)
- 2025-06-11: increased p99 alert threshold from 300ms -> 350ms after recurring false positives during model warmup.
- 2025-10-02: added Czar rotation to avoid duplicated customer communications when multiple teams are paged.

Owner and contacts
- Document owner: Avery Chen (SRE)
- Primary on-call group: embeddings-api-oncall (escalation route: #sre-embeddings, @pagerduty)
- Czar rotation channel: #czar-rotation (Slack)
- Status page maintainer: Platform Reliability team (status@redwood.ai)

Appendix: example evidence checklist (copy into ticket)
- [ ] Raw SLI timeseries (1h/6h/24h)
- [ ] Top 20 error traces (attached)
- [ ] Deploy manifests and diff (links)
- [ ] Affected API keys or customers list (anonymized if public)
- [ ] Post-deploy rollbacks or mitigations performed

Notes and best practices:
- Prefer conservative customer signalling for transient <15m blips; prefer proactive communication when customers depend on low latency for critical paths.
- Keep status page messages terse and factual; avoid speculation.
- Use the Czar role to reduce notification churn and ensure a single source of truth during SLO regressions.
